scenario.name: Kaspersky, Microsoft & Avast — Lazarus Group (Diamond Sleet): appid.sys Zero-Day & FUDModule Rootkit
scenario.shortSubtitle: Kaspersky GReAT / Avast / Microsoft · CVE-2024-21338 AppLocker Driver IOCTL & FUDModule DKOM Blindness
scenario.overview: Picture an international border crossing checkpoint with glass passport inspection booths, zig-zag queue stanchions, an X-ray luggage conveyor belt, and a striped crossing barrier. Approaching the international border crossing, a traveler steps up to the glass passport booth carrying a travel booklet with a subtly altered entry stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the luggage x-ray belt & barrier blending in with everyday guests, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station. A secondary customs officer cross-checks the border passport registry and catches a stamp serial number that was never issued by that embassy. In this scenario (CVE-2024-21338, Kaspersky, Microsoft & Avast, Lazarus Group (Diamond Sleet): appid.sys Zero-Day & FUDModule Rootkit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: opening a Handle to the Built-in Windows, then sending a Crafted IOCTL to Flip Kernel, then zeroing Out Kernel EDR Callbacks. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Opening a Handle to the Built-in Windows, then Sending a Crafted IOCTL to Flip Kernel, then Zeroing Out Kernel EDR Callbacks, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

details.description: Lazarus Group C2 server delivering the FUDModule rootkit and receiving exfiltrated R&D source code after EDR sensors are blinded.

stages.title: APPID.SYS KERNEL ZERO-DAY EXPLOIT (CVE-2024-21338)
stages.subtitle: Sending crafted IOCTL 0x22A018 to \Device\AppId to flip KTHREAD.PreviousMode
stages.description: Approaching the international border crossing, a traveler steps up to the glass passport booth carrying a travel booklet with a subtly altered entry stamp. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the luggage x-ray belt & barrier blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the border customs officer go about their routine. Because modern Windows blocks untrusted kernel drivers via Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE) and Microsoft’s Vulnerable Driver Blocklist, the attacker does not drop any third-party .sys file onto the disk. Instead, they elevate a user-mode process to LOCAL SERVICE privileges (required because \Device\AppId’s access control list only lets LOCAL SERVICE, rather than standard Administrators, open a communication handle to it) and open a device handle to Windows’ own built-in AppLocker driver: C:\Windows\System32\drivers\appid.sys. Abusing a pre-installed inbox Windows driver (appid.sys, Living off the Land in the Kernel) completely sidesteps HVCI / Vulnerable Driver Blocklist checks because appid.sys is an official part of the Windows operating system. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ APPID.SYS IOCTL 0x22A018 / ⇠#1 RET PreviousMode=0) from Node ① (#1 Lazarus (Diamond Sleet) C2) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Sysmon & Defender XDR Sensor).

stages.title: FUDMODULE V3 DKOM: BLINDING SYSMON, ETW-TI & EDR
stages.subtitle: Zeroing PspCreateProcessNotifyRoutine, ObRegisterCallbacks & EtwThreatIntProvRegHandle
stages.description: While the customs scanner checks only the outer cover of the passport, the forged interior page clears the glass booth and the striped crossing barrier swings upward. Here in Step 2 inside the border control, the intruder uses borrowed access inside the border control to slip closer to the passport glass inspection booth without disturbing the diplomatic sealed pouch lane. FudModule calls DeviceIoControl with control code IOCTL 0x22A018 (which invokes the internal function AipSmartHashImageFile inside appid.sys) and passes a crafted structure containing a spoofed function/object pointer (CVE-2024-21338). This tricks the kernel driver into decrementing the attacker thread’s KTHREAD.PreviousMode byte in kernel memory from 1 (UserMode, where Windows blocks the thread from touching kernel RAM) to 0 (KernelMode, telling the Windows kernel to treat every subsequent NtReadVirtualMemory and NtWriteVirtualMemory call from this thread as if it came from the kernel itself, granting unlimited Ring-0 memory read/write). When a thread calls NtWriteVirtualMemory, the kernel checks KTHREAD->PreviousMode: if it is 1 (UserMode), the kernel rejects any target address above 0x7FFFFFFEFFFF (protecting kernel space). Once CVE-2024-21338 flips PreviousMode to 0 (KernelMode), the thread can read and overwrite any address in the Windows kernel directly from user mode. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ BLIND SYSMON & ETW-TI / ⇠#2 ALERT EDR Blinded) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 appid.sys (AppLocker Driver)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Sysmon & Defender XDR Sensor).

stages.title: UNMONITORED KAOLIN RAT & LSASS CREDENTIAL DUMP
stages.subtitle: Dumping LSASS memory and deploying Kaolin RAT while EDR is blinded
stages.description: Rolling luggage smoothly off the X-ray conveyor into the secure arrival hall, the traveler crosses the border wearing an official-looking entry clearance. In this final step inside the border control, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station until the customs passport registry catches the mismatch. Instead of killing the endpoint’s EDR security service (which would immediately set off a "Sensor Offline" alarm on the SOC dashboard), FudModule uses its new kernel read/write access (Direct Kernel Object Manipulation, DKOM) to overwrite the kernel’s PspCreateProcessNotifyRoutine, PspCreateThreadNotifyRoutine, and ObRegisterCallbacks arrays with zeroes (erasing the kernel notification hooks that tell the EDR whenever a new process or thread starts) and disables EtwThreatIntProvRegHandle (shutting off Microsoft’s Kernel Threat-Intelligence telemetry feed so the EDR agent stays running with a green status light, but is completely blind and deaf). By surgically zeroing out the callback pointers registered by the security vendor’s kernel driver (.sys) and flipping the ProviderEnableInfo bit on the ETW Threat-Intelligence provider, Lazarus can subsequently dump LSASS and run malware with zero EDR alerts. In the documented Zeek / Suricata NDR exchange from appid.sys (AppLocker Driver) to FUDModule v3 DKOM Engine, FUDModule v3 DKOM Engine responds with ALERT Host/NDR Gap (confirming that the KAOLIN RAT C2 request succeeded on FUDModule v3 DKOM Engine and completing the final execution objective of Kaspersky, Microsoft & Avast, Lazarus Group (Diamond Sleet): appid.sys Zero-Day & FUDModule Rootkit). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ KAOLIN RAT C2 / ⇠#3 ALERT Host/NDR Gap) from Node ③ (#3 appid.sys (AppLocker Driver)) to Node ④ (#4 FUDModule v3 DKOM Engine), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Sysmon & Defender XDR Sensor).

detectionRule.title: Avast / Kaspersky GReAT — Lazarus FUDModule CVE-2024-21338 Rootkit
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule Lazarus_DiamondSleet_FUDModule_CVE_2024_21338 {
  meta:
    author = "Avast / Kaspersky GReAT"
    cve = "CVE-2024-21338"
  strings:
    $dev = "\\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\AppId" wide ascii
    $ioctl = { 18 A0 22 00 }
    $fn1 = "EtwThreatIntProvRegHandle" ascii
    $fn2 = "PspCreateProcessNotifyRoutine" ascii
  condition:
    uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and ($dev and $ioctl) or ($fn1 and $fn2)
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Apply the February 2024 Microsoft security update patching CVE-2024-21338 in appid.sys and enable Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI).

detectionRule.title: Network Firewall Egress Without Matching Endpoint Network Telemetry (DKOM Blindness)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
CommonSecurityLog
| where SourceIP == "10.10.40.15" and DestinationPort == 443
| join kind=leftanti (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where LocalIP == "10.10.40.15"
) on $left.DestinationIP == $right.RemoteIP
detectionRule.mitigation: Correlate perimeter NDR/Firewall connection logs against endpoint EDR network telemetry to detect hosts whose kernel callbacks have been blinded by rootkits.
